text:
Marta: Heads-up — Hydra (dedicated pool hydra-prod) reported rising 429s and token/Sec SLO violations after a marketing blast. Started ~09:12 UTC. Admission queue depth jumped.
Josiah: Seen the alerts. Can you paste the admission controller logs and Billing state? Wondering if burst credits were exhausted or auth delayed.
Marta: Quick logs: ```
[09:12:07] admission: enqueue 820
[09:12:12] admission: admit=false reason=burst_credit=0
[09:12:13] proxy: upstream_err=429 tokens=0
[09:12:20] autoscaler: desired=5 actual=3 scaling_disabled=false
```  Looks like credits hit 0 and scaler lagged.
Alex: I pulled the pool metadata — headroom policy is set to "min_reserved=2, headroom_pct=10" which for this workload was insufficient. Also saw noisy-tenant hnq-7 consuming long KV-cache insert cycles causing GPU thrash.
Sophie: Billing-bot shows delayed credit refill events for account hydra-inc. Reconcile timestamp: ```billing-bot: credits_replenish_requested=2026-03-03T09:11:58Z processed=2026-03-03T09:16:45Z``` so ~5m lag.
Josiah: So two factors: burst credits drained + billing processing delay + autoscaler reaction time. Any repro steps we can run to validate admission behavior? Need deterministic repro for engineering.
Alex: Repro steps I used locally against a staging pool (hydra-staging):
1) run a spike generator: `./tps-bench --concurrency 200 --rps 1600 --duration 300 --payload small`
2) watch admission logs: `kubectl logs -l app=admission -n infra | grep enqueue`
3) intentionally set headroom low: `redwoodctl pool update hydra-staging --min-reserved=1 --headroom-pct=5`
4) observe 429/queueing and autoscaler lag with `kubectl get hpa -w`
Alex: Attached sample `tps-bench` output and admission tail.
Marta: I also reproduced where a noisy tenant (hnq-7) was retaining large KV cache entries forcing evictions and increased inference latency. That prolonged token emission and reduced effective tps.
Josiah: Action items:
- Alex to open eng-runtime ticket with logs, repro steps, and FIFO of noisy-tenant traces. (owner: alex)
- Marta to reach out to customer hydra-inc about temporary throttling and ask for request pacing. (owner: marta)
- Sophie to check billing pipeline SLA and file ops ticket about the 5m refill delay. (owner: sophie)
- Engineering: consider raising default headroom for bursty pools and add a fast-path for credit refill race windows.
infra-bot: Created ticket ENG-6349 for autoscaler tuning (link: https://redwood/eng/6349)
Josiah: Thanks — I'll coordinate a postmortem and recommend short-term mitigations: increase headroom to 25% on hydra-prod, pre-warm workers, and add a temporary admission fallback to soft-throttle instead of hard 429s.
Marta: deploying headroom bump to hydra-prod now.
Alex: I'll include KV-cache metrics in the runtime dashboard and add a noisy-tenant alert on sustained cache miss growth.
Sophie: Billing ops acknowledged and will investigate backlog; will follow up in 2 hours.
Josiah: Closing slack thread once ENG ticket has triage notes. :white_check_mark:
